name: Lacertus Syndrome
definition: Proximal median nerve compression beneath the lacertus fibrosus near the elbow, causing forearm/hand weakness and activity-related symptoms.

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; ultrasound/electrodiagnostics may be supportive but can be normal.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, cartilage, tendon, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent objective weakness may require specialist decompression.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

patientEducation.summary: Proximal median nerve compression beneath the lacertus fibrosus near the elbow, causing forearm/hand weakness and activity-related symptoms.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, severe deformity, progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
